examples.en: I pay the rent one month in advance.
I prepaid three months of tuition at the academy.
This shop only takes customers who pay up front.
After I paid up front by card, I got a receipt.
I prepaid the hotel for the trip, so it is hard to cancel.
Is it cheaper if I prepay my phone bill?

explain: 값을 먼저 내는 건 '선불', 다 쓴 뒤에 내는 건 '후불'이에요. 말할 때는 '먼저 내다', '미리 내다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '선불 카드', '선불 요금제'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Paying first is 선불, and paying after use is 후불. In everyday speech people more often say '먼저 내다' or '미리 내다', while 선불 also appears as a noun, as in '선불 카드' (prepaid card).

examples.en: My grandmother gathers medicinal herbs in the mountains.
This herb is good when you drink it as tea.
They sell dried herbs at the market.
The smell of herbs filled the house.
I received a soap made from medicinal herbs as a gift.
Which herb is good for a cold?

explain: 약으로 쓰는 풀은 '약초', 한약의 재료가 되는 풀뿌리나 열매까지 넓게 부를 때는 '약재'라고 해요. '약초를 캐다', '약초를 달이다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: A plant used as medicine is 약초, while 약재 is the wider word for any ingredient of herbal medicine, including roots and fruits. It pairs with set verbs like '약초를 캐다' (gather) and '약초를 달이다' (boil down).

examples.en: The password has six digits.
Please check the number of digits in the phone number again.
When I calculate, I line up the digits.
Numbers with many digits are hard to read.
The number goes through as long as the digit count is right.

examples.ko: 일의 자릿수는 숫자 맨 오른쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: The ones digit is at the far right of the number.

explain: '세 자리 수', '두 자리 숫자'처럼 '자리'로 세는 말이 더 흔해요. '자릿수'는 비밀번호나 계산에서 칸이 몇 개인지 말할 때 쓰고, '자릿수가 맞다', '자릿수가 모자라다'처럼 말해요. 소리는 [자리쑤]로 나요.
explain_en: Koreans often count with 자리, as in '세 자리 수' (a three-digit number). 자릿수 is used for how many places a password or calculation has, as in '자릿수가 맞다' or '자릿수가 모자라다'. It is pronounced [자리쑤].

examples.en: This song is my own composition.
My friend sang me his own song on the guitar.
I want to enter the contest with my own song.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 자작곡이 많아서 인기가 있어요.
examples.en: That singer has many self-written songs and is popular.

examples.ko: 자작곡 한 곡을 완성하는 데 한 달 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to finish one original song.
Where can I listen to your original songs?

explain: 자기가 만든 노래는 '자작곡', 남의 노래를 다시 부른 건 '커버곡'이에요. '자작-'은 '자작시'처럼 직접 지은 것 앞에 붙고, 곡을 직접 만드는 사람은 '싱어송라이터'라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: A song you made yourself is 자작곡, while a song you sing again from someone else is a 커버곡 (cover). The prefix 자작- also appears in '자작시' (a poem you wrote), and a performer who writes their own songs is often called a 싱어송라이터.

en: drop out of school; leave school voluntarily

examples.en: My older brother dropped out of school last year.
That friend left school and is preparing for the equivalency exam.
Talk with your teacher before you drop out.

examples.ko: 정말 자퇴할 거예요? 부모님은 알고 계세요?
examples.en: Are you really going to drop out? Do your parents know?
I had to leave school because I was sick.

examples.ko: 자퇴한 학생도 다시 입학할 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can a student who dropped out enroll again?

explain: 스스로 그만두면 '자퇴', 학교가 내보내면 '퇴학'이에요. 일상에서는 '학교를 그만두다'라고 해도 되지만, 서류에서는 '자퇴서를 내다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Leaving by your own choice is 자퇴, while being sent away by the school is 퇴학. In daily talk you can say '학교를 그만두다', but on paperwork it is '자퇴서를 내다' (submit a withdrawal form).

examples.en: People in this village drink groundwater.
When it rains a lot, the groundwater increases.
We pumped up groundwater and watered the field.
Groundwater is cold even in summer.
The groundwater got dirty because of the factory.
This well is filled by groundwater.

explain: 땅 위를 흐르는 물은 '강물', 땅속에 있는 물은 '지하수'예요. '지하수를 파다', '지하수를 퍼 올리다'처럼 우물이나 펌프와 같이 많이 나와요. 마시는 물로는 '수돗물', '생수'와 비교해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Water flowing above ground is 강물 (river water), and water under the ground is 지하수. It is often used with wells and pumps, as in '지하수를 파다' and '지하수를 퍼 올리다', and compared with 수돗물 (tap water) and 생수 (bottled water).

examples.ko: 그 학생은 큰 잘못으로 퇴학을 당했어요.
examples.en: That student was expelled for a serious offense.

examples.ko: 퇴학은 학교에서 주는 가장 무거운 벌이에요.
examples.en: Expulsion is the heaviest punishment a school gives.
A notice of expulsion came to the house.
He barely escaped the danger of being expelled.
My friend said he is worried about being expelled.
How are expulsion and suspension different?

explain: 스스로 그만두면 '자퇴', 학교가 학생을 내보내면 '퇴학'이에요. '퇴학을 당하다'처럼 말하고, 얼마 동안만 학교에 못 오게 하는 벌은 '정학'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Quitting by yourself is 자퇴, and being removed by the school is 퇴학. You say '퇴학을 당하다' (get expelled), and a temporary ban from school is 정학 (suspension).

examples.en: This road is flat, so it is easy to walk.
They built a house on level ground.
That person's life was not smooth.
I am glad the work ended without trouble.
The path is level near the top of the mountain.
I heard it was easy, but it was quite hard.

explain: '평평하다'는 면이 고르다는 모양에 쓰고, '평탄하다'는 길이 고른 것 말고도 삶이나 일이 큰 어려움 없이 흘러가는 것에도 써요. 삶에는 '평탄하지 않았다'처럼 부정으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 평평하다 describes a surface that is even, while 평탄하다 also covers a life or task that goes along without big trouble. For life it is mostly used in the negative, as in '평탄하지 않았다' (it wasn't smooth).

examples.en: I found a shelter to get out of the rain.
The hut in the mountains became our refuge.
This library is a refuge for my mind.
When a typhoon comes, the school is used as a shelter.
The nearest shelter is the gym.
We spent one night at the shelter.

explain: 위험을 피해 가는 곳이 '피난처'예요. 재난 안내문에서는 '대피소'라는 말도 자주 보여요. 몸이 아니라 마음이 쉬는 곳을 '마음의 피난처'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: A place you go to escape danger is a 피난처. On disaster notices you will also see the word 대피소. It can also be a place where the mind finds rest, as in '마음의 피난처'.

examples.en: I take swimming lessons every weekend.
The class starts at seven in the evening.
Do you want to go to the yoga class together?
The instructor corrected my posture.
When this course ends, we take a test.
How much is the lesson fee per month?

explain: '수업'은 학교에서도 쓰지만 '강습'은 수영, 요가, 운전처럼 기술을 짧게 배우는 과정에 많이 써요. 배우는 것을 앞에 붙여 '수영 강습'이라고 하고, '강습을 받다'로 말해요.
explain_en: 수업 is used at school too, but 강습 is mostly a short course for learning a skill such as swimming, yoga, or driving. Put the skill in front, as in '수영 강습', and say '강습을 받다' to take lessons.

examples.en: There are two geese on the lake.
The goose is honking loudly.
My grandfather raises geese at his country house.
A blanket made of goose down is warm.

examples.ko: 공원에서 거위한테 쫓겨 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I was once chased by a goose in the park.
A goose is bigger than a duck.

explain: 거위는 오리와 비슷하지만 몸이 더 크고 목이 길어요. 겨울옷 안에 든 털을 말할 때 '거위털', '오리털'로 나눠 부르는 걸 자주 봐요.
explain_en: A goose looks like a duck but is bigger with a longer neck. On winter clothes you often see the stuffing named as 거위털 (goose down) or 오리털 (duck down).

examples.en: That person's outfit is a bit weird.
I heard a strange sound at night.
The dream was so bizarre that I still remember it.
I bought a weird-looking fruit.
Isn't the story of that movie strange?
People often tell me I am weird.

explain: '이상하다'보다 느낌이 세고 조금 기분 나쁘거나 낯설다는 뜻이 섞여 있어요. 사람의 모습이나 성격에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어서, 좋은 뜻으로 말하려면 '독특하다'나 '특이하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is stronger than 이상하다 and carries a hint of uneasy or off-putting. Using it for a person's looks or character can be rude, so for a positive tone say 독특하다 or 특이하다 instead.

examples.ko: 기차 맨 앞에서 기관차가 열차를 끌어요.
examples.en: At the front of the train, the locomotive pulls the cars.
I saw an old steam locomotive at the museum.

examples.ko: 기관차는 열차 맨 앞에 달려 있어요.
examples.en: The locomotive is attached at the very front of the train.
My child likes the toy locomotive best.
I heard the sound of a locomotive from far away.

examples.ko: 새 기관차로 바꾼 지 얼마 안 됐어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been long since they changed to a new locomotive.

explain: 열차를 끌고 가는 맨 앞 차량이 '기관차'이고, 사람이 타는 칸은 '객차', 짐을 싣는 칸은 '화물차'라고 해요. 평소에는 전체를 그냥 '기차'라고 부르는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The front car that pulls the train is the 기관차, the cars people ride in are 객차, and the cars carrying freight are 화물차. In daily talk people usually call the whole thing just '기차'.

examples.en: I hurt my leg and got a cast.
When do you take the cast off?
It is inconvenient to shower because of the cast.
I wrote my name on my friend's cast.
My friends drew pictures on the cast.
The cast feels very stuffy.

explain: 독일어 'Gips'에서 온 말이고, 병원에서는 '석고 붕대'라고도 해요. '깁스를 하다', '깁스를 풀다'처럼 말하고, 다친 팔이나 다리를 감싸면 '깁스한 다리'가 돼요.
explain_en: The word comes from the German 'Gips', and in hospitals it is also called 석고 붕대. You say '깁스를 하다' (get a cast) and '깁스를 풀다' (take it off), and a leg in a cast is '깁스한 다리'.

en: put in a cast; wear a cast

examples.en: I fell and had my ankle put in a cast.
My leg was in a cast, so I couldn't go to school.
The doctor told me to put my arm in a cast.
Climbing stairs with a leg in a cast is hard.
How long do I have to wear the cast?
If your wrist is in a cast, writing is hard.

explain: '깁스를 하다'와 같은 뜻인데, 짧게 말할 때는 '깁스했어요'를 자주 써요. 다친 곳이 목적어로 와서 '다리를 깁스하다'처럼 말하고, 풀 때는 '깁스를 풀다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '깁스를 하다', and the short form '깁스했어요' is common in speech. The injured part is the object, as in '다리를 깁스하다', and taking it off is '깁스를 풀다'.

examples.en: My dad is always making puns.
The wordplay in that ad is fun.
Stop the wordplay and let's talk seriously.
The title of this song is a pun.
My friend and I burst out laughing at a pun.
Because of the wordplay, it is hard to put into English.

explain: '말장난'은 소리가 비슷한 말로 웃길 때도 쓰고, 진지한 이야기를 피하면서 말을 돌릴 때도 써요. 뒤의 경우는 '말장난은 그만해'처럼 조금 불만스러운 느낌이에요. '아재 개그'는 비슷하게 썰렁한 농담을 말해요.
explain_en: 말장난 can mean a joke built on similar-sounding words, or dodging a serious topic with clever talk. In the second case, as in '말장난은 그만해', it sounds a little annoyed. 아재 개그 is a related kind of corny dad joke.

en: play on words; joke around with words

examples.en: I laughed while joking around with words with my friend.
The teacher made a pun and the students laughed.
He likes making wordplay.
I have no time for wordplay right now.
Please stop playing with words and give me an answer.
We sometimes made puns on each other's names.

explain: '말장난을 하다'와 같은 뜻인데 상황에 따라 느낌이 달라요. 친구끼리 웃자고 하면 가볍지만, 진지한 이야기 중에 '말장난하지 마세요'라고 하면 화난 말투가 돼요.
explain_en: It means the same as '말장난을 하다', but the feel depends on the situation. Between friends it is light, while '말장난하지 마세요' in the middle of a serious talk sounds angry.

examples.en: Kicking is important when you swim.
I practice kicks in taekwondo.

examples.ko: 아이가 힘껏 발차기를 해서 공을 멀리 보냈어요.
examples.en: The child gave a hard kick and sent the ball far away.
Kicking takes a lot of leg strength.
The opponent fell down with a single kick.
My legs hurt from kick practice.

explain: 발로 차는 동작을 말하며, 태권도와 수영에서 가장 자주 들려요. 수영에서는 '킥'이라고도 하고, 말할 때는 '발차기를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the kicking motion, heard most often in taekwondo and swimming. In swimming people also say 킥, and the common phrase is '발차기를 하다'.

examples.en: A nest hangs from the tree.
I found a bee nest under the eaves of the house.
This snack is shaped like a honeycomb.
You get honey from the hive.
Don't go near the nest.

examples.ko: 벌집은 작은 육각형 방으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: A honeycomb is made of small hexagonal cells.

explain: 벌이 사는 집은 '벌집'이고, 사람이 꿀을 얻으려고 만든 상자는 '벌통'이에요. 구멍이 많이 뚫린 모양을 '벌집'에 빗대어 '벌집이 되다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 뉴스가 나오자 온 동네가 벌집을 쑤셔 놓은 것 같았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 큰 소동이 나서 시끄럽고 정신없는 모습을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a place suddenly thrown into noisy confusion.

explain_en: The home of bees or wasps is a 벌집, while the box people make to collect honey is a 벌통. A thing full of holes is also compared to it, as in '벌집이 되다'.

examples.en: The car's bumper got dented.
I scratched the bumper while parking.
How much is the repair for the front bumper?
The bumper color is different from the car.
Please don't put stickers on the bumper.
The car behind bumped me lightly with its bumper.

explain: 차의 앞과 뒤 끝에 있는 부분이라 '앞 범퍼', '뒤 범퍼'로 말해요. 사고가 나면 '범퍼가 나갔다', '범퍼가 찌그러졌다'라고 하고, 놀이공원에서 부딪치며 타는 차는 '범퍼카'예요.
explain_en: It sits at the front and back ends of a car, so you say 앞 범퍼 and 뒤 범퍼. After an accident people say '범퍼가 찌그러졌다' (the bumper is dented), and the bumping ride at an amusement park is 범퍼카.

examples.en: I left my bags at the station storage.
What time does the storage office close?
I picked up my bag at the storage.
This storage costs five thousand won per day.
Let's meet in front of the bicycle storage.
I forgot my storage locker number.

explain: 역이나 공항에서 짐을 맡기는 곳은 '짐 보관소'나 '물품 보관소'라고 해요. 헬스장이나 학교에서 작은 칸에 물건을 넣는 곳은 '사물함'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: The place at a station or airport where you leave bags is a 짐 보관소 or 물품 보관소. The small lockers at a gym or school are called 사물함.

examples.en: He wanted to become a billionaire.
The president of this company is a billionaire.
Even a billionaire cannot buy time.
I am curious about a billionaire's life.
I saw a ranking of billionaires on the news.
What do billionaires spend their money on?

explain: '부자'는 돈이 많은 사람을 두루 말하고, '억만장자'는 그중에서도 손꼽히게 큰 부자라는 느낌이에요. 뉴스나 순위 기사에서 많이 나오고, '백만장자'는 그보다 한 단계 아래의 부자예요.
explain_en: 부자 is anyone with a lot of money, while 억만장자 feels like one of the very top rich. It shows up in news and rankings, and a 백만장자 is one step lower.

examples.en: Pine nut porridge is soft and good when you are sick.
I bought a bag of pine nuts at the supermarket.
Pine nuts are floating on the sujeonggwa.
I got a snack made of pine nuts as a gift.
I sprinkled a handful of pine nuts on the salad.
Pine nuts are nutty but expensive.

explain: 잣은 잣나무의 씨앗이라 고소하고 값이 비싼 편이에요. 잣죽, 수정과, 한과처럼 한국 음식에 자주 들어가고, 음식 위에 올리는 고명으로도 많이 써요. 호두보다 훨씬 작고 부드러워요.
explain_en: Pine nuts are the seeds of the Korean pine, rich in flavor and rather expensive. They go into Korean dishes such as 잣죽, 수정과 and 한과, and are often used as a garnish called 고명. They are much smaller and softer than 호두 (walnuts).

examples.en: The building extension work has started.
The school is noisy because of the addition.

examples.ko: 증축은 허가를 받아야 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only extend a building after getting a permit.
The house extension cost a lot of money.

examples.ko: 증축이 끝나면 교실이 두 개 늘어요.
examples.en: When the extension is done, there will be two more classrooms.
The hospital closed part of it for the extension.

explain: 있는 건물에 층이나 공간을 더 붙이는 건 '증축', 새로 짓는 건 '신축', 허물고 다시 짓는 건 '재건축'이에요. 공사 안내문과 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Adding floors or space to an existing building is 증축, building a new one is 신축, and tearing down to rebuild is 재건축. You see these on construction notices and in the news.

examples.en: Our house was small, so we added a room.
The school will extend the library.
You need a permit to extend a building.
We added on to this floor and enlarged the shop.
We put a window in the part we added.
After the hospital was extended, patients increased.

explain: 공사 용어라서 말할 때는 '넓히다', '더 짓다'를 쓰는 때도 많아요. 새로 짓는 건 '신축하다', 고치는 건 '수리하다'로 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It is a construction term, so in speech people often say 넓히다 or '더 짓다' instead. Building new is 신축하다, and repairing is 수리하다.

examples.en: This picture is my own creation.

examples.ko: 남의 창작물을 허락 없이 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use someone else's work without permission.
Creative works have copyright.
That work is popular overseas too.
Do you want to go to the exhibition of creative works together?
Would a work made by AI also have copyright?

explain: '작품'은 예술적으로 완성된 것이고, '창작물'은 직접 새로 만들어 낸 것이라는 점이 강조돼요. 저작권이나 인터넷 콘텐츠 이야기에서 '창작물'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 작품 stresses a finished piece of art, while 창작물 stresses that someone made it from scratch. It comes up often when talking about copyright or online content.

examples.en: Boxers adjust their weight to fit their weight class.

examples.ko: 체급이 다르면 같이 경기할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the weight classes differ, they cannot compete together.
That athlete moved up a weight class.
Weight classes are divided by body weight.
He won in the lighter weight class.
I control my diet because of my weight class.

explain: 복싱, 유도, 레슬링처럼 몸무게로 나눠 겨루는 운동에서 써요. '체급을 올리다', '체급을 내리다', '체급을 맞추다'처럼 말하고, 보통 사람의 몸무게를 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used in sports like boxing, judo, and wrestling where competitors are split by weight. You say '체급을 올리다', '체급을 내리다', and '체급을 맞추다', and you don't use it for an ordinary person's weight.

examples.en: Living alone in a foreign country is lonely.
He wandered through foreign lands for a long time.
The culture of another country feels strange at first.
Life in a foreign land was not easy.
When I go abroad, I miss my hometown's food.
I have a friend who married someone from another country.

explain: '외국'은 우리나라 밖의 나라를 두루 말하고, '타국'은 '남의 나라'라는 느낌이 있어서 고향을 떠난 쓸쓸함이나 오랜 타향살이 이야기에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '외국'을 훨씬 많이 써요.
explain_en: 외국 is the everyday word for any country outside your own, while 타국 means 'someone else's country' and fits stories of homesickness or long life away. In daily conversation 외국 is much more common.

examples.en: I apply foundation thinly on my face.
This foundation sticks well to the skin.
The foundation shade is too dark for me.

examples.ko: 새 파운데이션을 사려고 화장품 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the cosmetics shop to buy a new foundation.
I ran out of foundation.
I asked my friend to recommend a foundation.

explain: 피부색을 고르게 하는 화장품이고, 가게에서는 '쿠션'이나 '비비크림'과 같이 비교해서 골라요. 색은 '21호', '23호'처럼 호수로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a makeup product for evening out skin tone, and in shops people compare it with 쿠션 and 비비크림. Shades are given by number, like '21호' and '23호'.

examples.en: Pests appear a lot in summer.
I sprayed a repellent to keep the pests away.
Mosquitoes are pests that harm people.
Farmers have a hard time because of pests.
Pests gnaw at the crops.
This plant resists pests well.

explain: 사람이나 농작물에 해를 주는 벌레는 '해충', 도움이 되는 벌레는 '익충'이에요. 집에서는 보통 그냥 '벌레'라고 하고, '해충'은 농사나 안내문에서 '해충 방제'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Insects that harm people or crops are 해충, and helpful ones are 익충. At home people just say 벌레, while 해충 shows up in farming and on notices, as in '해충 방제' (pest control).

examples.en: Flowers bloomed in the flower bed in front of the apartment.
I take good care of the flower bed.

examples.ko: 화단이 넓어서 꽃을 많이 심을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The flower bed is wide, so I can plant many flowers.
Students look after the school flower bed.
The child picked a flower from the flower bed.
I rested sitting on the bench next to the flower bed.

explain: 땅을 따로 만들어 꽃이나 작은 나무를 심은 곳이 '화단'이고, 그릇에 심은 건 '화분'이에요. 학교나 아파트 앞에서 자주 보이고, '화단을 가꾸다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: A patch of ground set aside for flowers or small trees is a 화단, while plants in a container are 화분. You see them at schools and in front of apartments, and say '화단을 가꾸다' (tend a flower bed).

examples.en: A hedgehog has spines on its body.
My friend keeps a hedgehog as a pet.
The hedgehog got scared and curled into a ball.
I almost got pricked by a hedgehog's spines.

examples.ko: 고슴도치와 토끼 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like more, a hedgehog or a rabbit?
I saw a picture of a cute hedgehog.

explain: 고슴도치는 가시 때문에 속담에도 나오는 동물이에요. 비슷하게 가시가 있는 '호저'는 몸이 더 크고 가시도 길어서 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.example: 아무리 말썽쟁이여도 부모에게는 예뻐요. 고슴도치도 제 새끼는 함함하다고 하잖아요.
phrases.en: Even a hedgehog thinks its own young are silky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자식은 누구에게나 예뻐 보인다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning every parent thinks their own child is lovely.
phrases.en_equiv: every crow thinks its own young the fairest

explain_en: The hedgehog appears in a Korean proverb because of its spines. A 호저 (porcupine) also has spines but is bigger with longer quills, so it is a different animal.

examples.en: I put meat and green onions on the skewer.
I walked while eating skewers at the night market.
The skewer is hot, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 꼬치는 매운 소스를 찍어 먹어요.
examples.en: You dip this skewer in spicy sauce.

examples.ko: 친구가 나무 꼬치에 과일을 꽂아 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend put fruit on a wooden skewer for me.
It's two thousand won per skewer.

explain: '닭꼬치', '양꼬치', '어묵 꼬치'처럼 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 불러요. 음식도 꼬치이고 음식을 꿰는 막대도 꼬치예요. 셀 때는 '꼬치 하나', '꼬치 두 개'라고 해요.
explain_en: Put the ingredient first, as in 닭꼬치 (chicken), 양꼬치 (lamb), and 어묵 꼬치 (fish cake). 꼬치 is both the food and the stick it is threaded on, and you count them as '꼬치 하나', '꼬치 두 개'.

examples.en: It's the tail end of winter, so mornings are still cold.
I met my friend at the far end of the alley.
The closing part of that movie is moving.
I walked holding the hem of my skirt.
It rained at the very end of my vacation.
There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.

explain: 그냥 '끝'보다 천천히 끝나 가는 부분이라는 느낌이 있어요. 계절과 휴가 같은 때에는 '가을의 끝자락'처럼, 옷과 골목 같은 곳에는 '치마 끝자락'처럼 써요. '마지막'은 딱 하나뿐인 맨 뒤를 말해요.
explain_en: It feels like a part that is slowly ending, rather than a plain 끝 (end). It works for times, as in '가을의 끝자락' (the tail end of autumn), and for places or things like '치마 끝자락' (hem of a skirt). 마지막 means the very last one.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 어릴 때부터 제 단짝이에요.
examples.en: That friend has been my best buddy since we were little.
I ended up in the same class as my best friend.
We two are famous at school as a duo.
I fought with my best friend and I feel bad.
I want to meet a close friend at my new school.
A close friend understands you without words.

explain: '단짝'은 늘 둘이 붙어 다니는 사이라서 보통 한 명을 말해요. '베프'는 '베스트 프렌드'를 줄인 젊은 말투이고, '절친'은 '절친한 친구'를 줄인 말이에요.
explain_en: 단짝 is someone you are always with, so it usually points to one person. 베프 is a young-sounding short form of 'best friend', and 절친 is a short form of 절친한 친구 (a very close friend).

examples.en: You must not treat the two incidents as the same.
Please don't lump me together with that person.
Many people equate happiness with money.
The audience identified themselves with the hero.
It is rude to treat the two countries as the same.
I equate success with work, so I can't rest.

explain: 'A를 B와 동일시하다'처럼 목적어 하나와 '와/과' 말이 같이 와요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보이고, 말로는 '똑같이 보다', '같게 보다'가 쉬워요. 차이를 보는 '비교하다'와는 방향이 반대예요.
explain_en: It takes an object plus a 와/과 phrase, as in 'A를 B와 동일시하다'. It is common in news and writing, while in speech '똑같이 보다' or '같게 보다' are easier. It points the opposite way from 비교하다, which looks for differences.

examples.en: In basketball you need to grab rebounds well.
That player gets a lot of rebounds.
Tall players have the advantage in rebounding.
After a diet ends, it is easy for weight to bounce back.
The flow of the game changed because of the rebound.
The number of rebounds decided the team's win or loss.

explain: 농구에서는 슛이 빗나가 튕긴 공을 잡는 걸 말하고, 다이어트 뒤에 살이 다시 찌는 것도 '리바운드'라고 해요. 영어 'rebound'를 그대로 쓰는 외래어라서 한국어 말로 바꿔 쓰는 일은 드물어요.
explain_en: In basketball it means grabbing the ball that bounces off a missed shot, and weight coming back after a diet is also called 리바운드. It is an English loanword used as is, and Korean replacements are rare.

examples.en: My older brother is a good role model for me.
A teacher has to set an example for students.
Look at the sample and write the same way.
I'll take this as a lesson and be careful.
Read the sample sentence first.

examples.ko: 본보기는 눈에 잘 띄는 곳에 붙여 두세요.
examples.en: Put the sample somewhere easy to see.

explain: '모범'은 따라 해도 좋은 모습이고, '본보기'는 따라 할 대상뿐 아니라 일부러 보여 주는 견본에도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요. 나쁜 일을 한 사람을 '본보기로 벌주다'처럼 경고용으로도 써요.
explain_en: 모범 is a good model worth following, while 본보기 is wider: it can also be a sample shown on purpose. It is even used for warning, as in '본보기로 벌주다' (punish as an example to others).

examples.en: There is a crater at the top of Hallasan.
Water collected in the crater and became a lake.
I want to see a volcano's crater up close.
It is dangerous to go inside the crater.
There is a big lake in the crater of Baekdusan.
Smoke rose from the crater.

explain: 화산 분화구에 물이 고이면 '화구호'라고 해요. 백두산 천지가 가장 유명한 예예요. 달 표면의 둥근 구덩이는 '크레이터'라는 말을 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: When water collects in a volcanic crater it is called a 화구호 (crater lake), and Baekdusan's 천지 is the best-known example. For the round pits on the moon, the word 크레이터 is used more often.

examples.en: My father plays the saxophone as a hobby.
I like the saxophone because its sound is smooth.
I play jazz on the saxophone.
Is the saxophone hard to blow?
The saxophone sounds lower than the trumpet.
I want to learn the saxophone and the piano together.

explain: 악기마다 쓰는 동사가 달라서 색소폰은 '불다', 피아노는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'를 써요. '연주하다'는 어느 악기에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Each instrument has its own verb: 불다 for the saxophone, 치다 for the piano, and 켜다 for the violin. 연주하다 works for any instrument.

examples.en: When I catch a cold, I drink ginger tea.
Slice the ginger thinly and put it in.
Some people don't like the smell of ginger.
Ginger goes well with meat dishes.
Ginger is spicy, but it warms the body.
I boiled ginger and jujubes together.

explain: 생강은 '생강차', '생강청', '생강 쿠키'처럼 향과 매운맛을 내는 재료로 많이 써요. 마늘, 파와 함께 기본 양념으로 들어가고, 몸이 차거나 감기 기운이 있을 때 차로 마시는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: Ginger gives scent and heat in things like 생강차 (ginger tea), 생강청 (ginger syrup), and ginger cookies. It is a basic seasoning alongside garlic and green onion, and people often drink it as tea when they feel cold or a cold coming.

examples.en: Korea is a country short on water resources.
I use water sparingly to save water resources.
Managing water resources is an important job of the government.
When the climate changes, water resources change too.
A campaign to protect water resources was held.
I want to work at a water resources institute.

explain: '물'은 일상의 말이고 '수자원'은 사람이 쓸 수 있는 물을 나라나 지역 단위로 이야기할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '수자원 부족', '수자원 관리'처럼 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 물 is the everyday word, while 수자원 is used for the water people can use, talked about at the level of a country or region. In the news it appears as '수자원 부족' (shortage) and '수자원 관리' (management).
